name: OneGrid OneMeter
role: Software and hardware engineer: firmware, backend and dashboard
summary: Prepaid smart meter and charging-station logger for OneGrid Energies: an ESP32 touchscreen meter with an ATmega328 metering co-processor that works offline first, plus the Node.js backend and admin dashboard that run the fleet at meters.onegridenergies.com.
description: OneMeter controls the power at OneGrid charging stations and logs every device charged there, mostly OnePlastic solar lanterns. Version 3, the current one, pairs an ESP32 touchscreen (CYD) with an ATmega328 that runs HLW8032 metering, the relay and a watchdog over I2C. The meter keeps working without internet: readings and charging logs are stored on an SD card with an RTC, synced later with idempotent record IDs, and an offline list of device IDs lets staff log devices without a connection. Customers can be activated offline with time-based one-time codes. The Node.js/Express/MongoDB backend and a single-page admin dashboard manage meters, devices, top-ups, weekly deactivation, records with Excel export, analytics and signed firmware releases. The repository keeps every hardware generation, from the standalone v1 token meter to v3.
highlights: ESP32 touchscreen meter + ATmega328 HLW8032 co-processor over I2C, with a 4-second watchdog
Works offline first: SD-card storage, RTC timestamps and idempotent sync when the connection returns
Offline activation with TOTP codes and a replay guard; engineering PIN synced both ways and stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM)
Over-the-air updates signed with ECDSA P-256 in the admin's browser, with per-meter targeting and rollback reports
Admin dashboard: fleet overview, meter detail charts, device analytics by category, records with Excel export, light and dark themes, phone layout
Relay-fault detection and a configurable weekly deactivation schedule reported by each meter
